title: Redirect Python 2 docs to Python 3
question: How do I always land on the Python 3 docs instead of Python 2?
answer: Search results still link to Python 2 pages on docs.python.org, and the site has no setting to send you to Python 3; old pages only show a notice at the top and a version menu. The usermods script on this page catches any Python 2 docs page, at /2/ or /2.7/, and opens the same page under /3/, the current stable Python 3 docs. Python 3 pages are left alone. Without a script, change 2 to 3 in the address by hand.
prompt: Redirect docs.python.org Python 2 pages to the same page in the Python 3 docs.
details:
At `document-start` the script matches paths like `/2/library/os.html`, `/2.7/library/os.html` or a translated `/fr/2.7/...`, and replaces the version with `/3/`. It keeps the rest of the path and the `#anchor`, and uses `location.replace` so the Python 2 page is not left in the back history.

Some Python 2 modules were renamed or removed in Python 3 (`urllib2`, `ConfigParser`), so those pages land on a "not found" page. Pinned Python 3 versions such as `/3.12/` are not changed.

alternatives.title: Version menu
alternatives.body: Every docs page has a version menu in the header. Picking the current version opens the same page there.

alternatives.title: Edit the address
alternatives.body: Change `/2/` or `/2.7/` to `/3/` in the URL.
